problem:

Current State: The prevalent method of correction involves installing an orthotic device on the patient.
Pain Point: The complexity of the orthotic device makes it difficult to use. Its rigidity can cause discomfort or pain to the patient. Additionally, it occupies significant space, hindering the patient's mobility and causing inconvenience. Moreover, it does not guarantee accurate shaping.
Requirement: There is a need for a more effective method of correction.

lines.solution: realize the stretching construction like special controlled rod, put into the bone and growing on the length due the embedded micro-motor and miniature transmission.

problem:
Problem Scenario: Desktop fans are very essential in our life which can drive away the heat.
Current State: Traditional desktop fans with large, rubber-coated blades have been in use for many years.
Pain Point: Users are bothered by the noise generated by these fans. There's a risk of injury due to the exposed, large fan blades. Users experience discomfort due to irregular airflow patterns and occasional cold gusts.
Requirement: Develop a fan that operates more quietly to minimize disturbances, ensures user safety and produces a consistent and pleasant airflow, eliminating sudden gusts of cold wind.

lines.solution:
The inventor used the Coandă effect. The
"work stream" is pumped out through narrow fissures around the mouth of the entry plane and creates an additional stream "sucked in" at the entry point, and another additional stream "attracted at the exit point. The work stream is fed by the pump installed in the base of the fan through cavities in the round frame.

problem:
Problem Scenario: Metal sheets are intended for use in construction, including roofs, walls, and other structural elements. Durability and Reliability of Metal Sheets with Convex-Concave Cells are key factors.
Current State: Utilizes pressure molding and broaching methods to create metal sheets with convex-concave cell surfaces.
Pain Point: Unequal internal stresses lead to micro-fissures, compromising the structural integrity of the metal sheets. Micro-fissures make the metal sheets less durable, impacting their performance over time. The presence of micro-fissures reduces the reliability of these metal sheets for use in construction.
Requirement: Develop methods that minimize or eliminate uneven internal stresses during metal sheet production. Implement quality checks and controls to detect and prevent the emergence of micro-fissures. Aim to produce metal sheets that maintain structural integrity and reliability over extended use.

lines.solution: Inventors examined similar constructions created by Nature and reformulated the problem as "self-organization" of the cells making up the surface. Certain physical effects (hydro-vacuum pressing and particularly "selforganization" of cells under certain conditions) were used.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Developing a smaller, more efficient signal transmitter that integrates analogue and digital systems.
Current State:
The newly developed transmitter is significantly smaller than existing products, which allows strategic placement and uses less material.
Pain Point:
Due to its compact size, the transmitter cannot incorporate a standard cooling fan, leading to heat issues that affect transmission quality and speed.
Requirement:
Innovate a solution to dissipate heat effectively in the smaller transmitter without relying on a traditional fan, maintaining optimal performance.

lines.solution: Inventive Principle 16 of Partial or Excessive Action was applied on the selection of the microprocessors. The microprocessors were programmed not to work at the default maximum capacity at all times. With this, less heat is generated. With lesser heat generation, the performance of the device would not be adversely affected.

Two solutions were developed using Inventive Principle 17 of New Dimension. The circuit board is now designed to be multilayered. Each layer has the electronic components facing outwards towards the casing as shown in Fig. 4. Therefore more heat emitted by the electronic components is transferred to the casing which acts as a heat sink.

With Inventive Principle 10 of Prior Action, a thermal tape is placed over the electronic components that emit the most amount of heat. The thermal tape functions as a conductor that quickly transfers heat away.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Improving hand drying methods in public spaces.
Current State:
Existing hand dryers are slow and can scald hands, causing lines, while paper napkins are expensive and lead to clogged trash bins.
Pain Point:
The need for a hand drying solution that is both efficient and safe, avoiding the drawbacks of current dryers and paper napkins.
Requirement:
Develop a hand drying method that is quick, safe for users, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly, reducing queues and waste.

lines.solution: It is suggested to boost the speed of the air jets issuing from the hand drier to 640 km/h!
The air jets act like two razor-sharp brushes which "shave off" residual water from the skin
Introducing a useful property (removal of moisture) and removing harmful properties (scalding, slow operation).

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Optimizing large-scale submersible motor pumps for varying conditions in mine emergency drainage.
Current State:
These pumps are used in parallel for low lift, high flow drainage initially, and in series for high lift in narrow spaces later in mine rescues.
Pain Point:
Switching from parallel to series pump operation is time-consuming and complex, hindering rescue efficiency.
Requirement:
Develop a more efficient system for adapting pump operations to changing conditions in mine rescues, reducing installation time and improving overall efficiency.

lines.solution: Specific process is as follows: when the control valves KI , K3 is open and K2 is closed, the double-pump is independently parallel operation. On the one hand, the water flows from the upper pump suction port, after the upper pump impeller turbocharged, the water outflow from the pump outlet; on the other hand, the water flows from the lower pump suction port, after the lower pump impeller turbocharged, the water outflows from the pump outlet, finally converges to the total outlet. The submersible pumps lift is unchanged, but the flow is two times of the single pump flow. When the control valves KI, K3 is closed and K2 is open, the double-pump is serial operation. The water flows from the lower pump suction port, after the lower pump impeller turbocharged, the water outflows from the pump outlet, and enters the upper pump through the pipeline, then after the twice turbocharged by the upper pump impeller, the water reaches the total outlet from upper pump outlet and outflows. The submersible pumps lift is increased by one time.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Developing an improved stapling device for diverse nailing tasks.
Current State:
Existing staplers struggle with nail bending and deflection, especially in hard materials and with long nails.
Pain Point:
The stapler needs to quickly and accurately handle various nail types and sizes in different environments, balancing fast operation with the ability to pry, carry, and position nails both horizontally and vertically.
Requirement:
Create a stapler that is versatile, efficient, cost-effective, and aesthetically pleasing, able to handle different nails without increasing size or cost significantly.

lines.solution: The hitting pole and trestle are made into independent parts, with the mandrel moving axially along the trestle, enabling dynamic adjustment.
The trestle is designed as a tripod, and the hitting pole is divided into two parts (the hitting mandrel and the top cover), enhancing modularity and versatility.
A strong magnet is mounted in the mandrel's circular empty slot, allowing nails to be fixed magnetically for efficient operation.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Optimizing stamping/printing processes in the plastic injection market.
Current State:
Stamping machines are common but suffer from quality inconsistencies due to human operator variability, leading to resource wastage.
Pain Point:
Inefficiencies in placing and removing knobs on/from the stamping machine, and transferring them to the baking section.
Requirement:
Develop a more coordinated and efficient system, possibly using a single robot with dual manipulators and additional moving belts, to reduce human error and improve process quality and time efficiency.

lines.solution: an automatic system that can perform part of the work before arriving at the stamping station while using the wasted rotational energy of the mechanical system. One of the key components of this robot is using two fixed 90° arms (“prior action”). This separation helps the robot work twice as fast to improve the printing and stamping of the plastic pieces

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Developing a therapy vehicle for children with cerebral palsy (CP) that is engaging and effective.
Current State:
Existing therapy tricycles focus mainly on physical improvement but lack features that make therapy enjoyable and engaging for CP children.
Pain Point:
The mechanical design of current therapy vehicles fails to stimulate interest and enjoyment in CP children, lacking psychological considerations.
Requirement:
Create an innovative, friendly therapy vehicle that not only aids in physiological development but also incorporates fun elements to enhance personal dignity and enjoyment during treatment.

lines.solution: (1) to eccentrically connect the axle to a ground wheel(s) for gait motions in various degrees; (2) to provide available central connections to the axle and a ground wheel(s) for the traditional movement;(3) to provide adjustable mechanisms to accommodate diverse human statures; (4) to provide a seat belt to fasten user’s trunk; and (5) to provide foot brakes on the rear wheels to improve braking balance and safety.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Improving the dryer subsystem in a cylinder paper machine to enhance paper quality at higher speeds.
Current State:
The cylinder paper machine's productivity is increasing annually, necessitating higher operational speeds which affect drying times and paper quality.
Pain Point:
The increased speed results in insufficient dehydration time, compromising the quality of paper produced.
Requirement:
The dryer subsystem must be innovated to handle increased speeds without sacrificing quality, potentially by increasing the number or diameter of dryers.

lines.solution: Field action includes electric field, magnetic field and electromagnetism field, etc. This case can adopt a heating dryer using electromagnetic field, i.e., the dryer is heated by vortex that is produced by field acting on the dryer. The temperature of the dryer can be regulated by controlling the current and its frequency in the circuit. This structure can save the equipment for supplying vapour control easily, and its cost may not be too high.
The dryer is coated with a material that is sensitive to heat to increase the heat conduction. The coating can be restored.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Redesigning a metallic scooter wheel into a polymer variant.
Current State:
Metallic wheels are durable but heavy; polymers offer weight savings but have lower rigidity.
Pain Point:
Traditional methods of adding thickness and ribs to polymer designs do not translate well from metal parts and can hinder manufacturability.
Requirement:
Innovate the wheel's design using polymers, improving the geometric rigidity without imitating the metal part, ensuring manufacturability and maintaining functionality.

lines.solution: Applying this principle leads one to realize the wheel into two distinct parts to be assembled after the moulding process. The feasibility of such a solution has been confirmed by further studies; registered patents inspired by such a conformation are available

this produces the abandon of the plane web for a waved web, changing from two-dimesional to three-dimensional. The waved web increments both radial and lateral rigidity, and it can be manufactured with only one step of the mould

problem:
Problem Scenario: The need for extended battery life in notebook PCs.
Current State: High power consumption by components, especially the LCD monitor, reduces battery life.
Pain Point: LCD monitor, the largest power consumer, creates a contradictory relationship with battery efficiency and power management.
Requirement: Develop solutions to enhance LCD power efficiency without compromising display quality, balancing functionality with extended battery life.

lines.solution: As notebook PC LCDs typically use only one CCFL, the fundamental principles of backlight illumination may be changed to replace the CCFL with light emitting diodes (LEDs). A CCFL is shown at the top and LED at the bottom of Fig. 2. The LCD assembly can be broken out into principal components that include an upper diffuser sheet, prism sheet, lower diffuser sheet, reflector sheet, backlight module, and light guide. Light guide design and specifications vary based on backlight module type and structural design requirements. Applying density change principles, several (segmented) LEDs can be distributed evenly across the space vacated by the CCFL in order to achieve adequate, even illumination.

Variations in the external environment may be regularly referenced in order to adjust optimal notebook settings. Installation of a light sensor (intermediary) can enable notebook systems to adjust backlight brightness automatically and reduce LCD power consumption. Sensor sampling of environmental light levels can reduce or increase screen brightness to maximize user comfort and conserve power.

Computer use is often interspersed by periods in which a user stops work to rest or perform other tasks. A screen that remains on during these ‘‘down times’’ continues to drain the battery, wasting power and reducing battery efficiency. Installation of a thermal imaging sensor (body heat detector) can enable the notebook to run regular user presence checks. Once a user moves a designated distance from the notebook, an automatic response program can be implemented to reduce backlight brightness to the lowest setting or cut power to the LCD screen after a specified period of time has elapsed. This function requires the integration of appropriate application software to maximize power conservation efficacy.

problem:
Problem Scenario: The need for efficient and effective equipment maintenance in notebook PC manufacturing to ensure optimal operation and product quality.
Current State: Traditional maintenance approaches rely on estimates based on past data to predict equipment malfunctions, leading to either overly frequent or insufficient maintenance.
Pain Point: An overly conservative approach to maintenance increases costs and idle time, while an overly liberal approach leads to equipment wear and substandard production. Additionally, frequent maintenance contributes to environmental pollution and can disrupt production schedules.
Requirement: Develop a more accurate and efficient maintenance strategy that minimizes unnecessary downtime and costs, maximizes equipment lifespan, reduces environmental impact, and ensures consistent product quality.

lines.solution: Length of time taken by equipment to stray from normal operating parameters rather than length of time to breakdown should be used to set optimal preventive maintenance cycles. Such an approach will permit precise calculation of average values and standard deviations in order to make accurate decisions regarding preventive maintenance cycle length.

Regular/ daily equipment maintenance affected by equipment operators includes cleaning, oiling, spot checks, and ensuring critical screws/bolts are tight. Such selfmaintenance is guided by total productive maintenance (TPM) principles and methodologies with the objective of extending the period in which equipment runs within normal operating parameters in order to reduce preventive maintenance related expenditures and down time.

Irregular preemptive adjustments using an ‘‘intermediary’’ may be performed on equipment to help determine whether equipment has strayed from normal operating parameters. Taking SMT reflow oven adjustment as an example, oven temperature must be adjusted to the specific and distinct process temperature requirements of the chipsets/components in each product lot. Overheating will damage chipsets/components, while under-heating will result in the cold soldering of chipsets/components, which can significantly reduce process yields. Therefore, preemptive action is necessary to refine and adjust reflow oven temperature settings to ensure optimal performance and desired process yield. Thermal sensors should be installed to obtain readouts on oven temperature at each stage essential to ensure optimal temperatures profile.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Improving facility lighting for better defect detection in part inspections.
Current State:
Operators in the facility struggle to detect defects due to insufficient lighting, leading to quality issues later in the process.
Pain Point:
Additional lighting installed to enhance visibility increased energy costs, making it an unsustainable solution.
Requirement:
Develop a cost-effective and energy-efficient lighting solution that allows operators to effectively detect defects without significantly increasing energy consumption and costs.

lines.solution: increasing the illumination level for the whole workshop is not an ideal solution for the problem. It is sufficient to increase the illumination level of the area where only inspection tasks are done. Target operational area (inspection area) and the other areas can be independent of each other with the segmentation process between layout arrangement and illumination system. The same process can be applied to the segmentation of manufacturing and inspection areas

unnecessary lights can be determined with the investigation of different locations of facility. In this way energy saving can be achieved with the reduction of lighting accessories in those areas. Moreover, energy and lighting accessories may be transferred to required areas
providing different illumination levels for different location of the workshop with the help of segmentation and extraction processes

in case of separation of manufacturing and inspection tasks, the illumination level can be lowered at the manufacturing time and increased at the inspection time, which is held at only specific periods
motivation of the operators in detecting the defects is increased by employing a penalty system
chemical indicators that identify rust and similar defects and also give any damage to product can be used. Indicators change the colour in the event of defect and it becomes easy to see the defects

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Addressing operator fatigue in a batch production workshop.
Current State:
Operators manage multiple machines, leading to prolonged standing and movement, resulting in fatigue and increased accident risks.
Pain Point:
Implementing a seating arrangement reduced operator fatigue but led to increased intervention times and decreased production efficiency.
Requirement:
Find a solution to minimize operator fatigue without compromising productivity and efficiency in the workshop.

lines.solution: working environment of the operator should be analysed, then factors causing fatigue could be eliminated. Redesigning clothing and shoes of the operators, and rescheduling of working hours are a few samples
it is required to select and design a settling providing lesser walking distance and an inspection area
to improve the system when making loading–unloading operations automatically or to speed up failure detection process will decrease the fatigue with reasonable costs

problem:
Problem Scenario: Power supply system in notebook computers poses inconvenience for users.
Current State: Notebook computers have a power supply system consisting of a battery pack and a mains adaptor connected by two cables, one from the socket to the mains adaptor, and another from the mains adaptor to the notebook computer.
Pain Point: Assembling and disassembling the mains adaptor when near a socket is inconvenient for users. Carrying all the components during travel is also burdensome.
Requirement: Develop a more user-friendly power supply system for notebook computers that eliminates the need for assembling/disassembling the mains adaptor and simplifies portability for users.

Problem Scenario:
The ship faces a dilemma in balancing efficient transportation with the need to displace water during movement, leading to increased resistance.
Current State:
Increased engine power in the ship results in significantly higher water resistance due to its hull design, making speed enhancement challenging.
Pain Point:
The technical contradiction is that greater engine power, intended to increase speed, disproportionately increases water resistance. The physical contradiction lies in the hull's requirement to be broad for stability but narrow to reduce water resistance.
Requirement:
Develop a solution that allows for an increase in the ship's speed with only a minimal increase in engine power. This could involve redesigning the hull to minimize water resistance while maintaining stability, potentially using concepts from aerodynamics and hydrodynamics.

lines.solution: The “disruptive” hull of the ship was separated from the water using “necessary” elements separated from the ship’s hull – the hydro-foils. This is exactly the idea of the Russian inventor Rostislav Alexeyev who started the development of high-speed ships with hydro-foils at the beginning of the 1950 ‘ s

The challenge is to redesign a 500-passenger aircraft capable of both landing on a carrier and breaking the sound barrier, presenting unique engineering complexities.
Current State:
Current aircraft designs do not simultaneously meet these advanced operational capabilities due to inherent technical and physical limitations.
Pain Point:
The main technical contradiction lies in designing an aircraft large enough to carry 500 passengers, yet agile and robust enough to achieve supersonic speeds and carrier landings.
Requirement:
The objective is to develop a design solution that reconciles these conflicting requirements: maximizing passenger capacity while ensuring the aircraft's capability for supersonic speed and carrier-compatible landing.

lines.solution: Principle 15 is ‘dynamicity’, which is illustrated with various examples that can be linked to the concept of variable wing geometry as a possible solution.

In the production of liquid crystal screens, two thin, flexible glass sheets (each less than 1 millimeter thick and 2 meters in size) must be handled delicately to prevent breakage.

to use some copy of the sheet like mediator with a feature to hold the sheet on the whole upper surface (“a back”) and to be held to a lower surface of the upper platform.
Upper glass is chucked by glue S3. Glue can be temporarely brought on the glass out of the machine or enter from the capillaries in the upper platform. Glue can be brought not along entire surface. Glue could be removed back through the capillaries in the upper platform.

problem:
Problem Scenario: The objective is to design a skidding winch to enhance timber harvesting productivity, improve operator safety, and minimize environmental impact in areas where mechanized harvesting is constrained.
Current State: Current skidding winches face design trade-offs between blade width and frame width for stability and vehicle size, pulling power and cable strength, and cable length and strength.
Pain Point: Key challenges include balancing tractor stability with vehicle size to prevent damage to surrounding trees, ensuring sufficient pulling power without compromising cable integrity, and achieving optimal cable length that maintains strength.
Requirement: Develop a skidding winch that optimizes the balance between stability and size, pulling power and cable durability, and cable length and strength, to improve timber harvesting efficiency and safety while reducing environmental harm.

lines.solution: The blade was divided into a fixed part and two additional parts.

changed the degree of flexibility of the system using a double drum system, so that the stress generated during the pulling operation can be distributed on two cables. Both pulleys, and related drums, were positioned at the centre of the skidding winch to allow their use without affecting the stability of the tractor.
A protection for the cable was introduced to prevent cable breaks. Another proper “local quality” solution could be a swaged steel cable, which offers higher tensile strength for the same diameter.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Enhancing the efficiency of the post-machining process by reducing cycle time and operator fatigue during the removal of machined components.
Current State:
After machining, the removal of components is currently manual, leading to extended cycle times and increased operator fatigue.
Pain Points:
The key contradiction is the necessity of manual handling for quality assurance, which is inefficient and physically demanding for operators.
Requirements:
Develop a method to expedite the removal of machined components, aiming to minimize cycle time and reduce operator fatigue, while maintaining the quality of the process.

lines.solution: It was decided to place ejectors in bush shape so that after completion of the machining this intermediate operation (ejection) helped to lift the component, finishing the work within 3 seconds. By this, the operator fatigue is eliminated and the process time is also reduced

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Improving the machining process for a connecting rod, focusing on the post-boring stage to enhance efficiency.
Current State:
After boring, the connecting rod requires manual deburring and edge correction, a process that is time-consuming and causes operator fatigue.
Pain Points:
The contradiction lies in needing manual finishing which is slow and tiring, yet essential for quality.
Requirements:
Streamline the deburring and edge correction process to reduce time and operator fatigue without compromising quality.

lines.solution: Use a multi-storey arrangement of objects instead of a single-storey arrangement. Tilt or re-orient the object and lay it on its side. Use ‘another side’ of a given area. Here, the analysis on the possibility of doing the operation of removal of burr in the same setting is done. From another dimension principle, the operation of removing the burr was planned to be done in the reverse direction, i.e. Action from the bottom to top; for which the back chamfering tool was implemented, hence, the problem was solved, the productivity was improved and simultaneously the operator fatigue was reduced.

problem:
Problem Scenario: The shipowner use decision support tool for seafaring staff scheduling.
Current State:He is already using DMP(Decision Making Process) as decision support tool.
Pain Point: Expanding the fleet and operating vessels with different categories requires a new decision support tool with new constraints and objectives.The DMP used does not take into account aspects relating to Human resources management.
Requirement: A new decision support tool for seafaring staff scheduling is needed and it should take into account vessel category to be assigned in order to meet human resource requirements based on manning visa and identify the position(s) which each employee could get.

lines.solution: In this case we propose to change the degree of flexibility of the system, it means the possibility of creating a pool of employees who are trained in multiple skills, allowing for more flexibility in assigning them to different boats and roles.

This involves introducing elements flexibility into the system to decrees rigidity and complexity. In our case, it could involve creating a person or platform for workers that allowed to express their preferences for which team they would like to be assigned.

For our case, an intermediary could be a designated staff member who manages employee assignments and rotations on different boats. They serve as a point of contact for employees with assignment preferences, ensuring a balanced and stable team while addressing individual needs.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
The project involves designing a Smart Test Tube Rack (STTR) to improve the blood collection process in healthcare settings, addressing current inefficiencies and error-prone manual tasks.
Current State:
Currently, the blood collection process involves manually marking patient information on test tubes and selecting and confirming test tubes based on patient data, involving multiple stakeholders such as hospital management, nurses, patients, and their relatives.
Pain Points:
The process is time-consuming and susceptible to errors due to the manual marking of patient data and the selection of test tubes, along with challenges in integrating test tube management with hospital data systems, potentially compromising patient safety and data privacy.
Requirements:
The STTR design requires automation in test tube marking and identification to reduce manual input and errors, seamless integration with hospital data systems for accurate patient information, a user-friendly interface for nurses, robust privacy and safety measures for patient information, features to minimize incorrect test tube handling, and adaptability to various hospital environments and procedures.

lines.solution: Based on design principle 10, intelligent patients’ information recognition and the automatic test tube pickup and storage can be developed. Specifically, the improved design concept (IDC) should have the following functions: (1) automatically record patients’ information on test tubes; (2) automatically recognize the required test tubes and enable quick pickup; (3) lock the tubes to protect all tubes from misoperations; (4) remind the nurses with newly updated blood collection requirements. The prior actions would benefit the entire blood collection operations, provide comfortable and safe operations to nurses.
Based on design principle 12, the tube can be saved in protected environment instead of an opening environment.

Considering design principle 24, the test tube rack can be improved by linking it to the online data system for data sharing. In this way, the manual work on data input can be replaced by auto data collection and transmission. Therefore, a smart digital medical system with more specific medical process data, higher data synchronization degree, and improved medical service efficiency and precision can be expected. As mentioned above, the patients wonder about the process and re quirements of blood collection. To address this complaint, an interface for visualizing the process of blood collection should be developed. It can effectively increase the mutual understanding between patients and nurses.

Based on design principles 35, the shape of the tube rack can be redesigned. A rough design with a round shape (which provides comfortable and safer touch with no sharp edge and enablesthe rotation of test tubes for flexiblemovements), and the demountable construction of the rack and cover (for easier manufacturing, assembly and clean) was proposed.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
The project is centered on improving the design and functionality of a vice tool used in engineering applications for holding and processing steel tubes, addressing identified deficiencies in its current usage.
Current State:
The vice tool currently exhibits a linear joint with steel tubes, leading to significant bearing pressure on the tube during the application of large forces. This results in surface impressions and split marks on the tube. Additionally, long-term usage causes the rail of the vice to become swayed and unstable, affecting the tube's positioning accuracy and leading to processing warp. The vice's design also makes it challenging to rotate the tube or the vice itself when dealing with longer tubes, particularly in constrained spaces. Furthermore, the vice sometimes loosens under greater force, leading to clamping issues and a decline in processing quality.
Pain Points:
Key issues include the vice's inability to handle large forces without damaging the tubes, the loss of accuracy and stability over time, difficulties in maneuvering long tubes, and the vice's tendency to loosen under great force, compromising the clamping mechanism and overall processing quality.
Requirements:
The redesigned vice should distribute pressure more evenly to prevent tube damage, maintain stability and accuracy over prolonged use, facilitate easier handling and rotation of longer tubes in various spaces, and feature a more secure clamping mechanism that remains stable under greater forces to ensure consistent processing quality.

lines.solution: improve rail’s positioning accuracy and durability by changing manufacturing precision and rigid materials.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Addressing overcrowding at large-scale events like concerts and stadiums, where large crowds are both essential and a safety risk.
Current State:
Events regularly face safety and efficiency challenges due to overcrowding, yet large crowds are integral to their success.
Pain Points:
The contradiction lies in needing large crowds for a successful event while ensuring attendee safety and effective crowd management.
Requirements:
Develop solutions for safe and efficient crowd management at large events, without reducing crowd sizes.

lines.solution: Segmentation can be applied to the crowd problem by implementing barriers to divide the crowd into different sections. The barrier will avoid interference of the crowd in each section with the others. Segmenting the crowd may benefit us in different ways. A smaller crowd is easier to manage. Besides if people in one section collapse on each other, it will not affect the rest of the sections. As a result, the severity of pushing and trampling is decreased.

An idea generated from this principle is to have a building inside another building. If the overcrowding problem happens at the exits of a busy building, an exit tunnel which is built beneath the building might help (Figs. 5A and 5B). This is an effective method to avoid overcrowding and crushing of people in the case of emergency evacuations or even for normal yet overcrowded situations. By applying this principle, more space is provided to the pedestrians and a subgroup of people will be directed into a less crowded area.

the idea which comes to mind from this principle is to arrange the crowd into multiple floors (vertically) instead of a single floor (horizontally) as shown in Fig. 6. This change of dimension allows the accommodation of more people without affecting the area occupied by the building. However, the total area is increased as a result of the different structure dimension.

problem:
Problem Scenario:
Improving the packaging process for Chinese traditional medicine dropping pills, which are small, lightweight, and tend to have a sticky surface.
Current State:
Dropping pills are produced by dripping a liquid medicine mixture into a cooling liquid, forming solid-dispersoid pills. These pills are characterized by their small size (e.g., Cardiotonic pills are only about 3mm in diameter) and lightweight, due to the low dosage required. However, their production process results in a sticky surface.
Pain Points:
The contradiction lies in the pills' small size and sticky surface, which complicates the process of sorting (taxis) and bottling, creating bottlenecks in packaging.
Requirements:
Develop a packaging solution that can handle the small, lightweight, and sticky nature of dropping pills efficiently, reducing the bottleneck in sorting and bottling processes.

lines.solution: A new tumbling cylinder counting filling mechanical structure is put forward. In this structure, pick-off holes are equably distributed on the surface of tumbling cylinder and push-type plan using compress air is adopted. The sticky pills can be sorted out favorably. Pushed by compress air, the sticky dropping pills can easily fall into the small caliber bottle one by one. The project of multicenter filling can ensure the productivity of the packaging machine.

problem:
Problem Scenario: Traditional umbrellas, while effective in providing rain protection, present a contradiction between coverage and portability.
Current State: Standard umbrella designs typically prioritize increasing the rain coverage area, which often results in a bulkier and less convenient form factor for carrying and quick use.
Pain Point: This design contradiction leads to a user experience where the benefit of larger coverage comes at the cost of increased weight and volume, particularly inconvenient under frequently changing weather conditions.
Requirement: A redesigned umbrella is needed that offers substantial rain protection while being lightweight and easy to carry, thus improving the user experience.

lines.solution: the segmentation of the ribs (using rivet and stretcher) has solved the problem of increasing the area covered by the object and taking care of its portability. Consequently, this decreases the volume of the object when it is not in operation.

The ends of the ribs can be nested as with the pole and upper pole. This concept corresponds also with the separation principle in time: The object from one moment to another can be deployed to increase its radius and fulfill the new function of covering two individuals simultaneously

problem:
Problem Scenario:
The study focuses on enhancing the design of motorcycle roof shields for delivery riders, particularly in Malaysia, where motorcycles are popular.
Current State:
The existing roof shield designs have limitations such as poor aerodynamics and complex mechanisms, impacting rider performance and safety, especially in bad weather.
Pain Point:

Problem Scenario: In an Indian steel plant, the use of Electric Overhead Travelling (EOT) cranes for moving hot metal introduces significant safety hazards.
Current State: The plant has a safety department dedicated to preventing accidents and promoting safe operations.
Pain Point: The main issue is the improper engagement of the crane's hook, leading to potential safety incidents.
Requirement: Develop and implement improved safety protocols for correct hook engagement to reduce the risk of crane-related accidents.

lines.solution: Using composite materials for both hook and ladle there will be an improvement in stability while lifting objects.
asymmetry principle highlights the change of design of interacting objects (the hook and ladle) for better engagement among themselves.
Segmentation principle focuses on dividing objects to independent parts which are practically not possible in case of ladle and hook.

Mechanical vibration principle suggests provisions for vibrations to induce better engagement between interacting objects which is not advisable as the ladle carries huge tons of high-temperature molten metal, and vibration in any of the interacting objects may lead to spillage of molten metal and subsequently results in fatal incidents. 
Hence, the use of composite material and changing the design for both the hook and ladle are identified as possible solutions.

Problem Scenario: In road and bridge construction, prefabricated beams are used for efficiency. The SJL900/32 mobile bridge erecting machine, developed for tunnel beam erection, faces challenges due to the complex topography of construction sites. Requirement: Redesign or modify the mobile bridge erecting machine to enable direct loading of prefabricated beams from trucks on-site, while maintaining the machine’s stability and operational efficiency.

lines.solution: invention principle 13, inversion, reversing the position of an object, is as follows. The structure of the super system load beam truck is changed so that the overall height of the beam truck is reduced

invention principle 24, intermediary, using intermediaries to convey an object or an intermediate process, is as follows. A Hydraulic ram is installed between the rear truck and main girder. problem:
Problem Scenario: Railway turnouts, essential for train track switching, present significant risks due to rail discontinuity and high chances of derailment. The primary concern is the reduced maximum permissible speed on the diverted track, stemming from factors such as the lack of cant, small curve radius, and specific frog construction. Additionally, the problem of collisions between the wheel flange and the frog's nose during the transition phase is critical. This issue arises when the wheel traverses the gap of the crossing without being supported by the rails, moving from the direct rail to the crossing.
Current State: Trains are forced to decelerate substantially when navigating through turnouts, in stark contrast to their ability to maintain speed on main tracks. This slowdown is attributed to various elements, including the design of the turnout and the track conditions. The current design inadequately addresses the transition of wheels from direct rails to crossings, leading to potential wheel and track damage.
Pain Point: The foremost challenge lies in the obligatory reduction of train speed at turnouts, which adversely affects the overall traffic flow and efficiency on railway lines. This issue is further compounded by the risk of wheel-rail collisions at the frog's nose, posing a safety hazard and disrupting smooth train operation.
Requirement: The objective is to develop an innovative railway turnout design that overcomes these existing constraints, enabling safer and faster train movement at these pivotal junctions. The new design should specifically tackle the issues of wheel transition at crossings and enhance the overall efficiency and safety of rail traffic.

lines.solution: The objective, therefore, is to reduce the current gap by applying Principle 17 (Another dimension) and complementing the system with a mobile part, as indicated by Principle 15 (Dynamics), which is represented in red in Figure 10. This enhancementnot only minimises the existing gap, but also enables higher speeds in the railway operationThe advantage of using the mobile frog lies in its construction using higher-strengthmaterials, which are divided into several independent assembled pieces. This featureallows easy replacement in the event of wear, without having to remove the entire rail, inaccordance with principles 1 (Segmentation), 27(Cheap short-living objects), 13 (The other way round) and 35(Parameter changes)The proposed design optimises the use of space by applying Principle 17 (Another dimension), which makes it possible to construct a lighter and more robust partby applying Principle 8 (Anti-Weight). However, the most significant aspect to emphasiseis its independence from the common crossing, making maintenance much simpler to perform when replacement is necessary due to wear, in accordance with Principle 27 (Cheap short-living objects)

problem:
Problem Scenario: The main challenge in railway turnouts, critical for train track switching, is the inherent risk of derailment due to rail discontinuity and the reduced permissible speed on diverted tracks. The design of switch rails, particularly at points where wheels transition from direct rails to crossings, is problematic. This transition often leads to collisions between the wheel flange and the frog's nose, as wheels are not supported by rails in the gap of the crossing, increasing the risk of derailment.
Current State: Trains need to significantly reduce speed when passing through turnouts, a stark contrast to their speed maintenance on main tracks. This reduction, primarily due to the switch rail design and track conditions, leads to inefficiencies in rail traffic flow and potential damage to wheels and tracks.
Pain Point: The critical issue is the mandatory slowing of trains at turnouts, impeding overall railway line efficiency and safety. The technical conflict arises from the need to maintain speed for efficient traffic flow while ensuring safe wheel transition at switch rail crossings.
Requirement: The goal is to innovate switch rail design to address these challenges. The new design should allow for safer and faster train passage through turnouts, resolving the wheel transition problem at crossings, and thereby boosting the efficiency and safety of the railway system.

lines.solution: The system is based on the concept of the elastic switch rail (13-The other way round), which is coupled to either track without discontinuity and forged and stamped (35-Parameter changes) in the heel block to allow it to be welded to the rails that follow it inside of the turnout. The switch rail shall be subject to an up and down movement (19-Periodic Action), as well as a left and right turning movements (19-Periodic Action). Combining both movements, it shall be interlocked between the rail and the guard rail in order to prevent movement during the passage of the train. The aim of the up–down movement is to raise the switch rails (15-Dynamics) when the switch rail is moving sideways. The aim of this technique is to lighten the structure and prevent friction between the switch toe of the switch rail and the stock rails when the connecting plate on which the switch rails rest is raised.

13-The other way round: using the screw principle to precisely control the angle of the bicycle faucet, and the locking mechanism of the slide groove to control the upward and downward changes.

problem:
Problem Scenario: The primary challenge is reducing the number of motors in bidirectional peristaltic robots without compromising their adaptability to different pipe diameters and avoiding manufacturing difficulties.
Current State: Traditional peristaltic robots use three motors for movement, leading to complex control systems and manufacturing challenges due to space constraints and the need for multiple reducers.
Pain Point: The technical conflict lies in simplifying the robot's design by reducing the number of motors, which might adversely affect the robot's adaptability to varying pipe diameters and increase manufacturing complexity.
Requirement: The goal is to develop a peristaltic robot with fewer motors, simplifying design and production, while maintaining or enhancing its adaptability to different pipe sizes and operational efficiency.

lines.solution: In order to adapt to a small change in pipe diameter, according to inventive principle 1 (segmentation), we can divide the driven parts into rigid parts and flexible parts to adapt to the small change in pipe diameter. From Figure 14, due to manufacturing and assembly errors, when the legs of the robot extend outward, they may just touch the pipe wall, or they may not touch the pipe wall. According to inventive principle 1 (segmentation), the original rigid leg (follower) can be replaced by the combination of rigid parts and a flexible rubber mat, which can reduce the manufacturing accuracy requirements and save the manufacturing cost.

According to inventive principle 11 (Beforehand cushioning), a pre-compression spring can be applied to the leg to ensure stable support with the pipe wall. The greater the supporting force of the follower on the pipe wall is, the stronger the traction capacity is. In the actual environment, the pipeline interior may be uneven, and the adaptability of the rubber mat of the follower is limited. When the actual manufacturing dimensions and design dimensions of the support leg are very different, or when the actual inner diameter of the pipeline is larger than the ideal inner diameter, it will lead to the problem of insufficient support force. According to principle 11 of invention, we adopt a pre-compensation method to maintain sufficient initial support force by adding pre-compressed springs. Therefore, the designed follower has changed from using two parts to using three parts: a rigid body, pre-compression spring, and footpad. The use of pre-compression to pre-compensate the support force can not only adapt to the slight change in pipe diameter but also ensure sufficient support force.

Problem Scenario: The existing racks used to transport R/L side boards in the production of Upright Piano cabinets are causing transportation defects.
Current State: The current design of the racks does not adequately protect the side boards during transport, leading to damage and a subsequent increase in reworks.
Pain Point: The necessity to modify the racks to better protect the side boards has been identified as a critical factor contributing to production inefficiency and product defects.
Requirement: There is a pressing need to redesign the cabinet shelves to enhance the protection of side boards during transport, thereby reducing transportation defects and minimizing the rate of reworks in the manufacturing process.

lines.solution: Based on the condition of the industry and the wood working department, the chosen inventive principle is the intermediary (inventive principle no.24), i.e. the addition of material (foam) on the shelf so that there is no friction between the material from the wooden shelf and the backer on the cabinet which can cause clot (process). The divider and base of the shelf are equipped with foam to minimize friction between the cabinet and the wooden shelf when the operator picks up the cabinet. Then on the base of the shelf are also given holes that function so that the rest of the pieces of wood or backer can fall and not stick to the cabinet.
